newsitem.title: DUBAI: Arabsat stops French channel in decency dispute.
newsitem.headline: Arabsat stops French channel in decency dispute.

text.p: Arab satellite operator Arabsat said on Sunday it had stopped its transmissions of a French channel, saying it had showed a pornographic film and violated Islamic views of decency.

"We have stopped transmissions and as of today (Sunday) we consider the contract between Arabsat and Canal France International (CFI) finished. The contract is cancelled," a spokesman of the Riyadh-based company told Reuters.
"Yesterday they transmitted a pornographic film, and it was not the first time," he said. The spokesman said CFI had screened the programme despite repeated warnings by Arabsat.
Arabsat stopped transmitting the channel late on Saturday.
Arabsat, which operates satellite communications for Arab countries including television, telephone and data transmission, is jointly owned by 21 Arab states.
